description: Geology, meteorology, oceanography, and Earth's systems

earth_structure.crust: Outer solid layer; continental (30–50 km) and oceanic (5–10 km)
earth_structure.mantle: Solid rock but flows slowly; 2,900 km thick

plate_tectonics.theory: Earth's lithosphere is divided into tectonic plates that move

plate_boundaries.divergent: Plates move apart; new crust forms (e.g., Mid-Atlantic Ridge)
plate_boundaries.convergent: Plates move together; subduction or mountain building
plate_boundaries.transform: Plates slide past each other (e.g., San Andreas Fault)

rock_cycle.igneous: Formed from cooling magma/lava (granite, basalt, obsidian)
rock_cycle.sedimentary: Formed from compacted sediments (sandstone, limestone, shale)
rock_cycle.metamorphic: Formed by heat/pressure transforming existing rock (marble, slate, quartzite)

atmosphere_layers.troposphere: 0–12 km; where weather occurs; temperature decreases with altitude
atmosphere_layers.stratosphere: 12–50 km; ozone layer here; temperature increases with altitude
atmosphere_layers.mesosphere: 50–85 km; coldest layer; meteors burn up here
atmosphere_layers.thermosphere: 85–600 km; very hot; auroras occur here

weather_climate.weather_vs_climate: Weather = short-term atmospheric conditions; Climate = long-term patterns

climate_zones.tropical: Near equator; hot and humid year-round
climate_zones.polar: Ice caps and tundra; extremely cold

layers.epipelagic: 0–200 m; sunlight zone; most marine life

oceans.currents: Drive climate; include Gulf Stream (warm) and Labrador Current (cold)

natural_disasters.earthquakes: Caused by fault movement; measured by Richter scale or Moment Magnitude
natural_disasters.volcanoes: Opening in Earth's crust releasing magma; shield, composite, cinder cone types
natural_disasters.tsunamis: Ocean waves triggered by undersea earthquakes or landslides
natural_disasters.hurricanes: Tropical cyclones; form over warm ocean water; Saffir-Simpson scale
natural_disasters.tornadoes: Rotating columns of air; measured on Enhanced Fujita scale
